subject: co
fixes: f-co-taylor-series example: 'The true value is 2.0248457...' was wrong in the 7th decimal place (sqrt(4.1) = 2.024845673..., and the ellipsis implied truncated leading digits); now 'sqrt(4.1) = 2.02484567...'. P2(4.1) = 2.02484375, actual error 1.92e-6 and Lagrange bound 1.95e-6 were recomputed and are unchanged.

c-co-differentiability math: the example given for '|u| is differentiable at a zero of u iff u'(c)=0' was x|x|, which is not of the form |u|; replaced it with |x^3| (differentiable, derivative 0) versus |x| and |sin x| (not differentiable), and now explain x|x| separately (its difference quotient h|h|/h = |h| -> 0).

c-co-differentiability commonMistakes[1]: the item contradicted itself. It said to check whether the inside vanishes with a non-zero slope, then cited x|x| as differentiable, although the inside x of |x| has slope 1. It now uses |x^3| for the |u| test and treats x|x| as a factor cancelling the corner.

c-co-functions math (domain rules): 'a real power u^v with non-integer v is defined as e^{v ln u} and needs u > 0' contradicted the sqrt(u) rule (u >= 0, so u^{1/2} is defined at 0) and the cube-root functions x^{1/3} and x^{2/3}, which the formula and concept pages use on both sides of 0. The rule now applies only to irrational or variable exponents, and adds that rational powers follow the root rules (u^{1/2} needs u >= 0; odd roots such as u^{1/3} are defined for every real u).

f-co-lhopital latex and c-co-indeterminate-forms definition: 'provided the right-hand limit exists' was ambiguous because the same pages use 'right-hand limit (RHL)' for lim x->a+; both now read 'provided lim f'(x)/g'(x) exists (finite or +-infinity)'.
c-co-limits definition: the sequence-convergence definition lacked its quantifier; now 'for every epsilon > 0, |a_n - L| < epsilon for all sufficiently large n'.
f-co-differentiation-rules meaning: added the missing conditions to (log_a x)' = 1/(x ln a): x > 0, a > 0, a != 1.

f-co-convexity whenToUse: 'squared-error and log-loss objectives are convex' overgeneralised (false for, e.g., neural networks); now 'the squared-error loss of a linear model and the log-loss of logistic regression are convex in the parameters'.
c-co-single-variable-optimization math: 'a squared-error loss is convex in a single parameter' made specific: sum_i (theta - x_i)^2 or sum_i (y_i - w x_i)^2 (second derivative 2*sum x_i^2 >= 0).

c-co-indeterminate-forms gateRelevance: removed the unsupported claim 'They appear in 1-mark and 2-mark NATs and in MCQs whose options are close values such as e^k, 1, 0 and 1/2'. Both official DA limit questions in the repo (2024-Q60, 2025-Q32) are NATs, and there is no MCQ instance. It now reads 'They can be set as 1-mark or 2-mark NATs, or as MCQs ...'; 'Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for'.

c-co-continuity gateRelevance: removed the invented statistic 'Continuity is almost always examined together with differentiability'; now 'The syllabus names continuity and differentiability together, and one question can test both.'

c-co-maxima-minima gateRelevance: '1-mark MCQ' and '2-mark MSQ on a given polynomial' presented mark values as typical. The official polynomial MSQs carry 2 marks (2024-Q50, 2025-Q49) and 1 mark (2026-Q27), and the f'=0, f''>0 MCQ has a single instance (2024-Q15). Now 'Conceptual MCQ' and 'MSQ on a given polynomial'.

c-co-functions gateRelevance: 'It is usually examined together with continuity, differentiability or optimization rather than on its own' -> 'It can be examined on its own or combined with ...'; 'often an ML activation' -> 'for example an ML activation'.

c-co-limits gateRelevance: 'Limits are examined directly' -> 'can be examined directly'; 'often an infinity-minus-infinity form ... with a rounding instruction' -> 'for example ... rounded as the question specifies'.

c-co-taylor-series: gateRelevance 'Parity often makes the answer 0' -> 'can make', 'sometimes with a question about the error' -> 'possibly'; intuition 'the most useful single trick for exam questions on this topic' (unsupported exam claim) -> 'turns a question about a high-order derivative at the centre into a coefficient lookup'.

Frequency wording 'Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for' in all 8 co gateRelevance fields (c-co-functions, c-co-limits, c-co-indeterminate-forms, c-co-continuity, c-co-differentiability, c-co-taylor-series, c-co-maxima-minima, c-co-single-variable-optimization); content/exam/pattern.json supports no frequency claim.
